decisions.reason: In strips 1–2 (line 'וְנֶאֱמַר וּצְדָקָה תִּהְיֶה לָנוּ כִּי נִשְׁמֹר'), there is a visible word space between תִּהְיֶה and לָנוּ, and no maqaf. The only difference here is maqaf versus space, and the source shows a space.
decisions.uncertainty: low for the space vs. maqaf question. I could not confirm the dagesh in the lamed or the meteg at this print size. A and B have the same pointing on that word, so I did not decide it.

decisions.reason: In strips 4–5, the opening Kaddish paragraph ends 'קָרִיב, וְאִמְרוּ אָמֵן' followed by one dot, not a colon. Later paragraphs (strips 6–9) clearly end with 'אָמֵן:', so this print uses both marks and this one is a single dot.
In strips 5–6 the word is printed defectively, as ר with a holam dot and no vav ('וְיִתְרֹמַם'). Plene וְיִתְרוֹמַם is not printed.
Strip 6, line 3 opens with 'מִן־כָּל־בִּרְכָתָא': a separate מִן joined by maqaf to כָּל, then a second maqaf. A's contracted מִכָּל is not what is printed.
In the small-type congregational response in strips 6–7 ('קַבֵּל בְּרַחֲמִים וּבְרָצוֹן אֶת־תְּפִלָּתֵנוּ:'), a maqaf joins אֶת to תְּפִלָּתֵנוּ.
decisions.uncertainty: low for the maqaf. The meteg under ת in the small type is not clearly visible. A and B agree on it, so I did not decide it.

decisions.reason: In strips 8–9, the last Kaddish paragraph opens 'עֹשֶׂה שָׁלוֹם בִּמְרוֹמָיו', with ע carrying a holam dot and no vav. The same page also prints עוֹשֵׂה with a vav (in 'עוֹשֵׂה הַשָּׁלוֹם', strip 3), so spelling varies between occurrences and this one is defective.
